line: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 13 Aura Edition (2025, Lunar Lake) — current value pick
config_name: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 13 — Core Ultra 7 258V, 32GB LPDDR5x, 1TB SSD, 14" 2.8K OLED

battery.notes: 57Wh; CNET: 'more than twice the battery time' vs Gen 12; several hours longer than Gen 14.

price.notes: Clearance pricing as Gen 14 ships; CNET reviewed at US$2,474 new. CAD estimate.

offers.name: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 13 14" Business Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 7 258V - 32GB LPDDR5X - 1TB NVMe SSD - Windows 11 Pro - Black

reviews.quote: The little laptop is extremely light and long-running, making it a great pick for road warriors. But, Lenovo, you want how much for an OLED display?
Exceptionally lightweight yet sturdy build; Lengthy battery life; Stellar 2.8K OLED display; Best-in-class ThinkPad keyboard.
last year's [Gen 13] model... battery life is actually a few hours shorter [on Gen 14]

praises: Lunar Lake battery life is the best any X1 Carbon has had — easily a full workday with WiFi browsing
Sub-1 kg with the OLED panel; feels like a prototype in hand
2.8K 120Hz OLED is gorgeous for the price now that it is discounted
Aura Share file drop between Android phone and laptop actually works well
Quieter and cooler than the T14 under sustained compile jobs
complaints: OLED upgrade cost an absurd amount at launch — buy the discounted OLED tiers now
1080p webcam is disappointing given the price
Aura Edition feature bundle is mostly bloat users ignore
Only one USB-A port; dock or hub needed for legacy offices
Gen 14's repairability makes Gen 13 a worse long-term keep (soldered-heavy internals)

design_philosophy: The Lunar Lake-gen X1 Carbon that traded CPU cores for class-leading efficiency; now the notable value pick in the line at clearance pricing, beating the newer Gen 14 on battery.
rating_notes: Directly reviewed by CNET (OLED config). +1.5 battery vs Gen 14 per CNET's 'few hours shorter' note on Gen 14; −1 repairability (pre-Space Frame). Image URL is best-guess Lenovo CDN; site has fallback.
